title: KV cache scale & sensitivity probe: FP8/INT8/INT4 fidelity pipeline
creator: Ariana Soto
description: Goal: quantify end-to-end fidelity and operational trade-offs when applying aggressive KV cache compression profiles (FP8, INT8, INT4) across representative workloads and production cohorts. This ticket defines a repeatable pipeline for sensitivity sweeps, cohort-aware rollback thresholds, and an empirical decision matrix (latency, GPU memory saved, generation-quality delta). Rationale: prior probes focused on microbenchmarks (single-sequence MSE/PSNR). We need macro-level measures using real prompt distributions and generation behavior to assess safety of enabling lossy KV profiles in Dedicated/Private tiers.
experiment_plan: 1) Datasets/cohorts: a) RW-Chat-prod-sample-10k (user-chat style prompts across 12 languages), b) WikiText-subset-5k (long-context factual continuations), c) Codebench-1k (code completion-sensitive to exact tokens). 2) Models: base-v1 (FP16 baseline), opt-variant-1 (same architecture with runtime-compiled kernels). 3) Compression profiles: FP8 (E4M3), INT8 symmetric, INT4 blockwise 32B packing. 4) Sweep axes: sample retention fraction (100%, 75%, 50%), bit-depth, per-layer vs global quant, cohort-specific thresholds. 5) Runtime knobs: on-request dynamic fallback, cohort pinning, early-stop on regressed prompt families. 6) Compute targets: run each config across 3 seeds, 1000 prompts per cohort. 7) Instrumentation: token-level perplexity, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) on 0..1 scale, failure-rate (exact-match for code), end-to-end latency P50/P95, GPU memory delta (MiB), and quality regressions flagged by eval harness. 8) Acceptance heuristics: no cohort should have >1.5% absolute drop in semantic-similarity vs FP16 baseline and code exact-match loss <0.2% for production rollout candidates.
initial_results_summary: Preliminary runs (small-scale): FP8 E4M3 reduced KV memory by ~38%-42% and increased P95 latency by +2-6ms (due to dequant pipeline), typical embedding cosine delta around -0.006 (within target for RW-Chat), perplexity change +0.8% on WikiText. INT8 showed ~55% memory reduction with embedding delta -0.02 and occasional topk shifts for open-domain completions; code cohort saw a 0.9% exact-match regression (too high). INT4 blockpack saved ~70% memory but produced visible degradation on long-coherence tasks: embedding delta -0.06 and perplexity +5-8%; unacceptable for code and technical chat cohorts. Notably, per-layer quantization (only quantizing KV in middle 6 layers) yielded much of the memory benefit (~45%) while reducing quality impact vs global INT8. These numbers are aggregated from 3 seeds, RW-Chat 1k subset runs.
decisions: Proceed with FP8 E4M3 as 'candidate default' for conversational cohorts with cohort pinning and dynamic fallback enabled
Defer global INT8 rollout; pursue hybrid per-layer INT8 where we quantize only KV of middle transformer blocks
Block INT4 for production until we have per-request quality gating and a per-prompt fallback vector
Add a canary pipeline in Console to expose regression counts and cosine-delta distributions by cohort
Schedule a security review only if KMS-integrated compression keying is introduced (not in current plan)
